question: When only the time grid of the SAME reconstructed input changes, does a model that performs a nonlinear update at every observation produce a grid-dependent representation? Does a model with an exact linear input-integration stem and nonlinear updates only on a fixed physical-time clock add anything beyond fixed-grid resampling and prior work?
pilot_record: Before this file: 5 pilot trainings on the DEV split only with non-registered seed 99 (G_foh1 lr 2e-3 and 5e-3, G_tf1 lr 1e-3, G_nrde4 lr 2e-3 twice). Test data was not evaluated. Findings: dev accuracy plateaus near 0.96 by epoch 3; lr 2e-3 and 5e-3 equivalent; the NRDE baseline needed two fixes (logsig scaled by train RMS instead of std, because the time increment has std 0; drive divided by sqrt(dim) and LayerNorm before the head). Logs: results/pilot/.

data.signals: raw inertial signals, 9 channels, 50 Hz, windows of 128 samples (2.56 s, 50% overlap), physical time t_i = i/50 s, window span [0, 2.54] s
data.split: official subject-disjoint split: 21 train subjects / 9 test subjects. Dev = 4 train subjects drawn with numpy default_rng(2026) -> subjects [1, 6, 22, 25] (1402 windows); train 5950 windows; test 2947 windows
data.normalization: per-channel mean/std over all train+dev windows and time points (affine, commutes with the reconstruction rules)
data.independent_unit: test subject (9). Windows of one subject overlap by 50% and are not independent. Training seeds are not data units and are reported separately.

reconstruction_and_query_rules.foh: X(t) = linear interpolation of the knots on [t_0, t_{n-1}], constant hold outside
reconstruction_and_query_rules.zoh: right hold X(t) = x_i on (t_{i-1}, t_i] (the hold implied by h_k = Abar(dt_k) h_{k-1} + Bbar(dt_k) u_k)
reconstruction_and_query_rules.clock: tau_j = j * Delta_c, j = 1..J, J = floor(2.54 / Delta_c); Delta_c in {0.02 s (r=1), 0.08 s (r=4)}; independent of the observations
reconstruction_and_query_rules.clock_output: y_j at tau_j depends only on X restricted to [0, tau_j]; sequence readout = uniform mean over j
reconstruction_and_query_rules.perobs_output: y_k at every knot t_k > 0; readout = time-weighted mean with weights (t_k - t_{k-1}) / 2.54
reconstruction_and_query_rules.virtual_vs_measured: every knot carries a measured flag; virtual knots are placed on the reconstruction and are never counted as measurements; downsampling and dropping act on measured knots only

training.selection: best dev accuracy over epochs (native grid only)
training.train_grid: native 50 Hz grid only (no grid augmentation in the main arm)

groups_note: On the native grid the clocked and per-observation rules of G_foh1, G_zoh1 and G_none1 are the same function (clock ticks = native knot times; checked numerically), so each pair is trained once and the fixed-clock ablation is an inference-time switch on identical weights.

lossless (FOH): foh_rand (127 virtual knots at uniform random times)
real downsampling: down2_reknot (down2 path re-knotted with virtual knots at native times)
missing observations: drop50_reknot (same drop pattern as drop50, virtual knots at native times)
conditions.rng: per-window numpy default_rng([condition_seed, window_index]); identical for every model

metrics.accuracy: per condition; mean over 3 seeds; 95% CI by cluster bootstrap over the 9 test subjects (2000 resamples, seed 0) of the seed-mean
metrics.consistency: relative logit change ||z_cond - z_native||_inf / ||z_native||_inf per window (median, p95) and prediction flip rate vs native
metrics.fp64_exactness: max relative logit change on 256 test windows in float64 for foh_m2, foh_m4, foh_rand, zoh_m2 and down2_reknot vs down2
metrics.artifact_share: for lossy conditions: |F(down2) - F(down2_reknot)| / |F(down2) - F(native)| (same path, different knots / total change); zero by construction for path functionals
metrics.cost: scripts/cost_har.py on an otherwise idle machine, 1 thread: preprocessing seconds per window (raw knots -> model inputs) and forward seconds per window (batch 64), medians of 3 repeats on 512 test windows for native, foh_m4, down2, drop50; parameter count; training seconds per epoch from the logs (measured under 4-process contention)

hypotheses.H1_exact (engineering): Every path-functional model (P1, P4, B_point_clock1/4, B_binmean_clock4, B_patch_clock4, B_tf_clock1, B_tfpatch_clock4, B_nrde_clock4, B_rformer_clock4) has float64 max relative logit change <= 1e-10 under foh_m2, foh_m4, foh_rand, and float32 flip rate <= 0.1% under these conditions.
hypotheses.H2_core: Each per-observation model (A1_foh_perobs under foh_m2/m4/rand; A3_zoh_perobs and B_dtonly under zoh_m2, which is lossless for their own right-hold input rule) has median relative logit change >= 1e-3 (>= 100x the float32 floor) in float32 AND float64. PRACTICAL relevance additionally requires flip rate >= 0.5% or |accuracy change| >= 0.5 pp in at least one of these conditions.
hypotheses.H3_stem_bilinear: B_bilin_clock4 (not exact) shows relative logit change >= 1e-4 under foh_m4 (descriptive).

decision_rule.G1_beats_simple_resampling: P4_foh_clock or P1_foh_clock beats EVERY simple-resampling baseline (B_point_clock1, B_point_clock4, B_binmean_clock4, B_patch_clock4, B_tf_clock1, B_tfpatch_clock4) whose measured cost (prep + forward per window, native) is <= 1.5x its own, by >= 1.0 pp mean accuracy over the lossy conditions {down2, down4, drop30, drop50, drop70}, with the subject-bootstrap 95% CI of the difference excluding 0, and is no worse than -0.5 pp on native.
decision_rule.G2_not_prior_work: The literature check finds no prior work with overall overlap 'substantial' or 'full' for 'exact input integration + nonlinear updates on a fixed clock', AND the close-work baselines (B_nrde_clock4, B_rformer_clock4, B_bilin_clock4) do not come within 1.0 pp of P on the same lossy mean.
decision_rule.verdict: GO only if G1 AND G2. Otherwise NO_GO (gain explained by simple resampling or prior work). The answer to the core question (H2) is reported separately from GO/NO_GO.

secondary_descriptive: FS1 FlowState probe (real published model; Apache-2.0 weights ibm-granite/granite-timeseries-flowstate-r1 revisions v1.0 main and r1.1): real series ETTm1 (column OT). Lossless 2x/4x refinement by FOH virtual knots with scale_factor s/r; real 2x/4x downsampling with s*r; forecasts compared at common physical times; relative change of forecast and of the last backbone state. FlowState is called refinement-consistent if the relative forecast change is <= 1e-3.
AUG arm (only if the main arm finishes within budget): B_dtonly/A3 and P1/B_point_clock1 trained with grid augmentation; descriptive.

budget.cpu: 4 cores, no GPU (GPU gate records NOT_RUN)
budget.on_budget_exceeded: stop launching; mark missing runs NOT_RUN(TIMEOUT); no partial aggregates reported as complete

stop_conditions.S1_bug: If H1 fails for any path functional, stop and fix the implementation before any scientific reading.
stop_conditions.S3_no_sweep: No hyper-parameter sweep beyond the pilot; one shared setting per family.
